doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

chapter: Jackson, Medgar Evers and high school band
title: Booty Harriton's nosebleed at a white prom gig
summary: Griffin finishes the story of his high school band's baritone player Booty playing a white junior high prom, and they talk about 'Rhythm' changes for dancing.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: high school and obviously this girl thought he was a white guy playing in a black band. So she got up in front of him, and he played the baritone, he played [scats]. And she got in front of him and started dancing erotically and exotic — and Booty got so excited his nose started to bleed and he never stopped. He never stopped playing. He had a white shirt on, ‘cause we all wear — and he just played and blood was running down on his shirt. And I always made a joke of him laughing, I said man, Booty, you probably would have had a heart attack if your nose didn’t bleed. We had so much fun.
I think that’s a marvelous story and I love the fact that you can remember that he was playing [scats].

Yes. In those days we didn’t have a band you know. And — I mean bass. So he was the bari, he carried the bass. And it was “Blue” and we played it, and all the songs back in those days has “Rhythm” changes [scats]
in at 36:20 So all of those songs had that “Rhythm” changes and you just name any little song back then that that worked.
Yeah. And that 6/8 feel. That’s what you get to get the people on the dance floor.
